1. Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon — adjust upward bias by 1–3% for the first 5–10 days.

2. After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 2–5% in the 3–7 day window following a spike.

3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if 30-day history shows a clear downward trend, forecast should be slightly below the recent mean; if upward, slightly above.

4. Forecast lags true price movements by 1–3 days — shift forecast 1–2 days forward for short-term (1–7 day) horizons.

5. Model underestimates volatility in low-price regimes — increase forecast by 1–3% when price is below 85% of recent 30-day average.

6. Avoid overfitting to recent high prices — if last 5 days are above 90, reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 5 days to prevent over-optimism.

7. For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates the peak — cap forecast at 10% above the 30-day moving average to prevent runaway spikes.
